==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|deceave||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}} From {{inh|en|enm|deceyven}}, from {{der|en|xno|deceivre}}, from {{der|en|la|dēcipiō||to deceive; beguile; entrap}}, from {{m|la|dē-||from}} + {{m|la|capiō||to seize}}; see [[captive]]. Compare [[conceive]], [[perceive]], [[receive]]. Displaced native {{cog|ang|beswīcan}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/dɪˈsiːv/}} * {{hyph|en|de|ceive}} * {{audio|en|En-us-deceive.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|iːv|s=2}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[trick#Verb|trick]] or [[mislead]]. #: {{ux|en|It feels painful to begin seeing clearly, that you’ve been '''deceived''' by the very people and institutions you trusted to guide you.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1829|author=w:Edgar Allan Poe|chapter={{w|Tamerlane (poem)|Tamerlane}}|title=Al Aaraaf, Tamerlane and Minor Poems|passage=I know—for Death, who comes for me
From regions of the blest afar,
Where there is nothing to '''deceive''',
Hath left his iron gate ajar, […]}} #* {{quote-journal |1=en |date=April 26, 2012 |author=Tasha Robinson |title=Film: Reviews: The Pirates! Band Of Misfits : |work=The Onion AV Club |url=http://www.avclub.com/articles/the-pirates-band-of-misfits,73064/ |page= |passage=Hungry for fame and the approval of rare-animal collector Queen Victoria (Imelda Staunton), Darwin '''deceives''' the Captain and his crew into believing they can get enough booty to win the pirate competition by entering Polly in a science fair. So the pirates journey to London in cheerful, blinkered defiance of the Queen, a hotheaded schemer whose royal crest reads simply “I hate pirates.” |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130528104958/http://www.avclub.com/articles/the-pirates-band-of-misfits%2C73064/ |archivedate=28 May 2013}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2016|author=[[wikipedia:Ryan Holiday|Ryan Holiday]]|title=[[wikipedia:''Ego Is the Enemy''|Ego is the Enemy]]|page=146-147|passage=This is why the Zen philosopher Zuigan is supposed to have called out to himself everyday:
{{smc|“master”
“yes, sir?”}}
Then he would add:
{{smc|“become sober.”
“yes, sir.”}}
He would conclude by saying:
{{smc|“do not be '''deceived''' by others.”
“yes sir, yes sir.”}}
Today, we might add to that:
{{smc|“don't be '''deceived''' by recognition you have gotten or the amount of money in your bank account.”}}}} ====Synonyms==== * See also [[Thesaurus:deceive]] ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|deceivability|deceivable|deceivance|deceiver|deceivous|redeceive|undeceive|deceivingly |flatter to deceive|self-deceive|what a tangled web we weave when first we practice to deceive}} ====Related terms==== * {{l|en|deception}} * {{l|en|deceptive}} * {{l|en|deceit}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|trick or mislead|mislead|gaslight}} * Albanian: * Altai: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Belarusian: * Breton: * Bulgarian: * Burmese: * Catalan: * Cebuano: * Chinese: * Comorian: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Gallurese: * Georgian: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kabuverdianu: * Kapampangan: * Kazakh: * Khmer: * Korean: * Kurdish: * Kyrgyz: * Lao: * Latin: * Latvian: * Ligurian: * Lithuanian: * Luganda: * Macedonian: * Māori: * Middle English: * Mongolian: * Nepali: * Norwegian: * Old Avestan: * Old English: * Oromo: * Pennsylvania German: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Romansh: * Russian: {{t+|ru|обма́нывать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|обману́ть|pf}} * Sanskrit: * Sardinian: * Sassarese: * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tajik: * Tamil: * Telugu: * Thai: * Tibetan: * Turkish: * Turkmen: * Tuvan: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Uyghur: * Uzbek: * Vietnamese: * Zazaki: {{trans-bottom}} ====Further reading==== * {{R:Webster 1913}} * {{R:Century}}
